subject: Cross-region hosting qualification & next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Anna Koval <anna@medicodata.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T16:15:00Z
Subject: RE: Post-call: hosting fit and residency constraints

Hi Anna,

Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Requirements I captured:
  * EU-only residency for patient-level inference (no PII leaving EU)
  * APAC users need aggregated analytics / read-only logs (no raw PII)
  * KMS integration: EU-managed keys preferred
- Hosting fit options (high level):
  * Hosted API (EU-region endpoints) — fastest to prod if we can guarantee EU-only routing and disable cross-region fallback
  * Dedicated (reserved GPU in EU) — predictable throughput, customer-isolated pool; can support EU KMS
  * Private (VPC/on-prem) — full data residency/isolation; longer lead time and procurement

Open questions for MedicoData that affect recommendation:
1) Monthly avg requests and peak TPS (est tokens per request)
2) Are you required to have EU-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for model input/process? HIPAA/SOC2 specifics?
3) Procurement timeline and whether you can onboard Dedicated vs Private within Q1 2027

Attach: hosting_matrix_v2.pdf (pdf) — a matrix comparing tradeoffs and typical lead times.

Suggested next step: 30-min alignment call Weds 24 Nov (US mornings / EU afternoon). If you can share the TPS numbers and procurement timeline before then we'll map to an optimal path (Hosted with strict routing vs Dedicated vs Private).

Thanks,
Soojin
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachment: hosting_matrix_v2.pdf (pdf)
From: Anna Koval <anna@medicodata.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: John Perez <john.perez@medicodata.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: RE: Post-call: hosting fit and residency constraints

Thanks Soojin — useful recap. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

On 2026-11-21T16:15:00Z Soojin Lee wrote:
> - Requirements I captured:
>   * EU-only residency for patient-level inference (no PII leaving EU)

To confirm: EU-only is a hard requirement for any patient-identifiable inference. We cannot accept a fallback that could route inference to the US.

For APAC: the ask is to surface aggregated analytics for product/usage dashboards. Those logs must be pseudonymized and only contain aggregated counts — no raw patient text.

Questions from procurement (John is cc'd):
- Can Hosted API be configured to strictly enforce EU-only inference endpoints and also integrate with our EU KMS? If not, we need pricing and lead time for Private VPC.
- What are typical lead times for Dedicated vs Private (ballpark)?

We can give TPS numbers by EOD tomorrow. Our procurement timeline is tight — aiming for initial contract by end of Q1 2027. If Private is required, we need an estimate of the procurement window and any support you provide for on-prem install (agent/ops playbook).

Thanks,
Anna Koval
Head of Platform
MedicoData
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Anna Koval <anna@medicodata.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T18:10:00Z
Subject: RE: Re: RE: Post-call: hosting fit and residency constraints

Anna — thanks, that's clear and very helpful. Short answers up front, then action items below.

1) Hosted API EU-only behavior: we can provision EU-region endpoints and a routing policy that enforces EU-only model endpoints; by default Redwood can disable cross-region fallback for your account so requests will not be routed outside EU. However, KMS integration with customer-managed keys in EU is currently supported in Dedicated and Private; Hosted with customer KMS is a limited program (we've done a handful of pilots). We can surface a Hosted KMS path but it will require additional legal + security steps.

2) Lead times (ballpark):
- Hosted (EU endpoints): hours-days to enable access once account is set and security checks are done.
- Dedicated (reserved pool in EU): 4–6 weeks typical (procurement + capacity allocation).
- Private (VPC or on-prem): 8–12+ weeks depending on on-prem requirements, network approvals, and whether you choose a managed vs self-hosted package.

3) Private/on-prem support: we provide an ops playbook, a deployment runbook, and dedicated SRE onboarding for initial rollout (separate professional services).

Action items and owners:
- Anna / MedicoData: share monthly avg requests + peak TPS + avg tokens/request (due EOD tomorrow)
- Soojin (me): send a short hosting decision matrix (attached) + EU VPC/KMS FAQ document; recommend a go/no-go threshold for Hosted vs Dedicated based on TPS and KMS requirement
- Ben: provide commercial checklist and estimated pricing delta for Dedicated vs Private (Ben to follow up)
- Lauren: help prioritize security checklist items for Hosted KMS pilot

Attach: redwood_eu_vpc_kms_FAQ.docx (docx) — outlines KMS options, encryption at rest, audit logs, and required documentation for Hosted KMS pilots.

Proposed follow-up: Wed 24 Nov, 16:00 UTC (30 minutes) — I'll set a calendar invite for the time that works best for MedicoData.

Soojin
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_eu_vpc_kms_FAQ.docx (docx)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-21T19:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Cross-region hosting qualification & next steps

Looping in commercial notes — quick internal note:

- If MedicoData can accept Hosted with EU-only routing and no customer-managed keys, the procurement timeline is ~1–3 weeks (contract + security review).
- Dedicated adds a premium (~20–35% depending on commit) and ~4–6 week lead time. Private has higher TCO and longer onboarding; propose initial PoC on Dedicated in EU while we run Private sizing in parallel if KMS is non-negotiable.

I will prepare a short pricing delta sheet and send before EOD tomorrow so Soojin has numbers for the Wed call.

Ben Carter

Redwood Inference
